### Per-screen HUD reticle publishers: screen index at state+0xF8 — the deterministic gate (STATIC, 2026-07-04)

The ordinary crosshair does NOT go through `is-scope-visible?` at all. It is
spawned by the per-screen HUD publisher family over `g_PerScreenPlayerHudState`
(`0x143EF1E30`, 0x100 stride):

- `0x14135A650` — spawns/kills the `ss-hud-reticle` process, publishes
  `reticle-show-time` / `update-reticle-aspect`. Called from `0x1413B42E0` with
  `&g_PerScreenPlayerHudState[32 * idx]`.
- `0x14135AF20` — sibling publisher (also spawns `ss-hud-reticle`, publishes
  `total-ammo` etc.), called from `UpdatePlayerHudAimingAndWeaponAccuracyPublishes`
  (`0x1413571B0`).
- `0x14135C050` — blindfire reticle publisher, hardwired to screen 0 via the
  fixed aliases `qword_143EF1F20` (= state+0xF0 of screen 0) / `qword_143EF1F28`
  (= state+0xF8 of screen 0).

**Key field:** the screen/slot index lives at `state+0xF8` (decompiled as
`*(a1+248)`). Three mutually consistent proofs:
1. `0x14135A650` calls `GetRetainedPlayerEntityBySlot(*(a1+248))`.
2. It reads the slot's Joypad as `g_LocalPlayerInputManager_Ptr +
   0xBF0*(*(a1+248)+2)` — exactly the confirmed slot→joypad mapping
   (slot 0→joypad 2, slot 1→joypad 3 from `PLAYER-INPUT-BIND`).
3. The screen-0-only publisher `0x14135C050` uses the fixed `+0xF0/+0xF8`
   aliases of the first array element.

**Consequence + fix (implemented):** the duplicated crosshair is the SCREEN-1
(puppet) publisher spawning its `ss-hud-reticle` process onto the single shared
viewport. Mod gate in `teleport_hook.cpp`: hook `0x14135A650` and `0x14135AF20`,
skip the publish when `*(state+0xF8) != 0` (`hud_state_is_non_primary_screen`) —
weapon- and ADS-independent. Falsifiable prediction: peer holds aim (any weapon)
→ receiver shows puppet aim pose, `RETICLE-HUD gated: screen!=0` /
`RETICLE-AIM-HUD gated: screen!=0` lines appear, NO crosshair on the local
viewport; the local player's own crosshair (screen 0) is unaffected. Status:
**CONFIRMED** (runtime 2026-07-04 PID 22372/11672: crosshair no longer
duplicates; `RETICLE-HUD gated: screen!=0` present).

### Runtime 2026-07-04 (PID 22372/11672): screen-index gate CONFIRMED for crosshair; two new issues — native-fire ProbeKick crash + sniper-scope puppet vanish

**Crosshair dup: CONFIRMED FIXED** by the screen-index gate above.

**Issue A — receiver crash on fire (CONFIRMED cause = native Fire replay):**
Receiver `11672` took `EXCEPTION code=0xC0000005 rva=0x152CB38 fault=0x108
rcx=0xAF50064B819E0000` (non-canonical pointer). `0x14152CB38` is inside

the button-pulse path, which runs the game's own fire logic with the puppet's OWN
valid aim state. Predict: firing any weapon no longer crashes the receiver;

update `sub_140C193A0`, consumer `sub_140C149A0`). The scope-visible gate only

### Performance: game-thread logging file open/close is the primary stutter source (2026-07-04)

**Investigation of reported severe lag.** Ruled OUT by static review:
- All heavy per-frame diagnostic probes default OFF: `g_enemy_health_probe`,
  `g_hp_sys_probe`, `g_enemy_freeze_selftest`, `g_charmgr_dump_periodic`,
  `g_enemy_sync`, `g_client_damage_relay`, `g_local_animation_mirror_test`,
  `g_drive_screen1_cam` = all `false`. `send_enemy_states`/`monitor_hp_kill_selftest`
  early-out when their toggle/watch is unset, so no character enumeration by default.
- The per-frame update hook `hooked_update` is installed on the **NadineBuddy
  vtable slot** only (`g_nadine_vtable[kUpdateSlot]`), not a shared Actor/Character
  vtable, so it fires for ~1-2 objects/frame, not every NPC. `net_tick` is
  internally clock-gated (send @60Hz, weapon @100ms, etc.).
- The reticle/scope HUD gate hooks are cheap (one `readable_bytes` + one dword read;
  logs rate-limited to 1000ms).

**PRIMARY CAUSE (CONFIRMED static, pending live A/B):** `log_line` opened AND closed
the log file (`std::ofstream` app-mode ctor/dtor = `CreateFile`+`CloseHandle`) on
the **game thread for every single line**. 381 call sites; during active co-op the
rate-limited diagnostics (`JOYPAD3-ANALOG`, `REMOTE-ACTIONS`, `REMOTE-DRIVE`,
`PLAYER-INPUT-UPDATE`, `PRE-CONSUMER-MOVE`, …) still emit dozens of lines/sec across
two instances. Each open under the Defender-watched Desktop path costs
milliseconds, and cost grows with file size (587 MB observed) → per-frame hitching
that gets worse the longer you play. Classic injected-mod stutter.

**Fix (implemented):** persistent single log HANDLE opened once per process, guarded
by an SRWLOCK, `WriteFile`-append only (no per-line open/close). Master switch
`g_logging_enabled` (VK_HOME toggle) for a zero-I/O run. This removes the expensive
open/close syscall + Defender scan from the game thread's hot path.

**SECONDARY suspect (not yet changed — needs care):** `readable_bytes` runs
`VirtualQuery` (kernel syscall) at 280 call sites, many per-frame guarding pointer
derefs. At high call counts this is a few ms/frame. Caching is unsafe (it's the
guard against freed/unmapped memory — a stale cache returning "readable" would
crash), so any optimization must reduce call COUNT by hoisting repeated checks in
the hot paths (input_scale_copy dest=3, drive ticks, send_local_player_state), not
cache results. Left for a targeted follow-up.

**A/B tools for live confirmation:** VK_HOME = logging off (isolates file I/O);
VK_END = `g_dll_inert` full pass-through (isolates ALL mod per-frame logic). If
VK_HOME alone restores smoothness, logging was the cause; if only VK_END does,
the remaining cost is `readable_bytes`/per-frame logic. Status: **STATIC** (cause
+ fix), **HYPOTHESIS** (severity) pending user A/B.

### Performance ROOT CAUSE: memory exhaustion (16 GB RAM, two 10 GB instances), not the mod (2026-07-04)

**Measured live (both instances running, PID 26176/22200):**
- Physical RAM: **15.9 GB total, 0.3 GB free.**
- Commit charge: **54.9 / 59.5 GB** (~39 GB pushed to the page file / disk).
- Each `tll.exe`: **~10.6 GB private commit**, but **working set only ~3 GB
  resident** each (6.1 GB combined resident out of 21 GB committed). The OS has
  hard-trimmed ~15 GB of the games' memory to disk because there is no physical RAM
  to keep it. `\Memory\Pages/sec` ~100 at idle (spikes under gameplay).
- Also resident: `vmmem` (WSL/Debian for the MCP server) ~4 GB commit.

**Conclusion:** the severe stutter is **memory-pressure paging**, not the mod's
CPU/logging. Two 10 GB AAA instances cannot both stay resident in 16 GB RAM, so
gameplay constantly hard-faults paged-out memory from disk. Per-process CPU was
only 17–20% of all 16 threads and no mod thread pegs a core (aux_input_thread
sleeps 15 ms; recv threads block; heavy probes default off). The earlier VK_HOME/
VK_END A/B was invalid: **VK_HOME was already the `g_dll_inert` toggle** in
aux_input_thread, and the logging toggle I added collided with it.

**Remediation (not a code fix):**
1. Don't run two 10 GB instances on 16 GB — the real deployment is two PCs via
   Steam Remote Play Together (already the roadmap target).
2. If testing on one PC: lower each instance's texture/quality/resolution to shrink
   the working set; close other consumers; free the WSL `vmmem` 4 GB
   (`wsl --shutdown`, stops the MCP server) while playtesting.
3. Add RAM (16 → 32 GB) for two-instance local testing.

**Mod-side hygiene done anyway:** `g_logging_enabled` now defaults **false** (zero
log file I/O on the game thread); F11 re-enables when diagnostics are needed;
persistent log handle retained. Fixed the VK_HOME triple-binding. Status:
**CONFIRMED** (root cause = RAM paging, measured).

### Performance CONFIRMED (2026-07-04): per-frame VirtualQuery in readable_bytes was the stutter root cause

**Runtime A/B, single instance (PID 6276):** un-injected the game runs at full
speed; injected with the old build it stuttered badly at LOW CPU (~19%) and
near-zero game GPU usage (main thread waiting, not computing) with RAM/disk NOT
saturated. Swapping `readable_bytes` from `VirtualQuery` to the lock-free SEH
page-probe **eliminated the lag** (user-confirmed "именно оно").

**Mechanism:** `VirtualQuery` acquires the process address-space lock. The game's
asset-streaming / allocator threads hold that lock continuously, so calling
`VirtualQuery` from our game-thread pointer guards (280 `readable_bytes` sites,
dozens+/frame) contended on it and **blocked the main thread** each frame → low
CPU, stalled frames, smooth-without-mod. Fix: `readable_bytes` fast path touches
one byte per page under SEH (no syscall, no VAD lock), reporting the readable
extent up to 0xB000. Toggle `g_readable_bytes_fast` (VK_NEXT) keeps the old
VirtualQuery path for A/B.

**Corrections to earlier perf notes this session:**
- The "logging open/close is the primary stutter source" note was WRONG as the
  *primary* cause — logging was a minor secondary cost. The persistent-handle log
  fix + default-off logging are still worth keeping, but the dominant per-frame
  cost was VirtualQuery contention.
- The "memory exhaustion" note applies ONLY to running TWO 10 GB instances on
  16 GB RAM (a separate, real constraint for local two-copy testing); it was not
  the single-instance lag.
Status: **CONFIRMED**.

### Sniper scope leak: is-scope-visible is a process-global; gate on LOCAL ADS (STATIC, 2026-07-05)

**Path fully mapped.** `SniperReticleManager_QueryScopeVisible` (`0x140C177F0`,
kScopeVisibleQueryRva `0xC177F0`) resolves the **process-global**
`ss-hud-sniper-reticle-manager` (string `0x142A03110`, the string's ONLY xref) via
property registry `dword_146466FE0` and queries its `is-scope-visible?` property.
Returns bool = draw the full-screen sniper scope reticle. Prologue confirmed
(`48 89 5C 24 08 … 55`) — the co-op mod's detour installs correctly. Sole caller =
`ReticleManager_Update` (`0x140C193A0`), itself in the main HUD chain
`HudUpdate_Main` (`0x140C149A0`); it operates on the PRIMARY screen
(`g_PlayerHandleForHudPublish` = local player, `ResolveScreenRouteEntityByIndex(0)`).

**Why it leaks:** the property is global — it goes true when EITHER the local
player OR the co-op Second player enters scoped-rifle ADS. On the single physical
viewport, a Second-player scope therefore draws the sniper reticle on the local
screen (user: "снайперский прицел дублируется **без виньетирования**" = the flat
HUD scope reticle, not the full ADS scope-camera composite).

**Why Cursor's gate produced zero gated frames:** the prior condition
`remote_player_ads_active() && !local_player_should_show_scope()` depended on
resolving `retained_player_object(1)+0x1548` (the Second player's ADS flag) at the
exact query frame — fragile; if that object/read didn't line up, the gate never
fired. The hook itself was installed (prologue matches), so the failure was the
runtime condition, not the detour.

**Fix (implemented, STATIC):** replace the condition with a robust, Second-player-
independent one: on the primary viewport the global scope is legitimate ONLY when
the LOCAL player is scoped, so force the query to 0 when
`player_ads_active(retained_player_object(0))` is false (local `Player+0x1548==0`).
This cannot suppress the local player's own scope (local ADS → allowed) and does
not depend on reading the Second player object. Log: `SCOPE-VISIBLE gated: local
player not scoped (Second-player leak)`.

**Falsifiable prediction:** copy-1 snipes → on copy-2 (local Nadine not scoped) the
sniper reticle no longer draws, and the log shows the gate line each ~1 s while
copy-1 holds scope; copy-2's OWN sniper scope (when its local player scopes) still
works. If the reticle still draws WITH the gate line present, then is-scope-visible
is not the sole draw signal and the residual path is the scope CAMERA (Cursor's
"Chloe vanishes" hypothesis) — next target. Status: **STATIC**.

### Co-op wrong aim/shot direction: fire uses the per-screen aim camera, not the body quat (STATIC, 2026-07-05)

**Symptom:** the Second player "aims and shoots in the wrong direction."

**Root cause (static, PlayerFireController_Fire 0x140E2C730):** the shot/aim
direction is resolved from the FIRING PLAYER's own screen camera, not from its body
orientation. At 0x140e2d57e the fire core does
`ResolveScreenRouteEntityByIndex(*(controllerOwner+0x4010))` (0x4010 = the player's
screen/slot index, same field the per-screen HUD publishers use) then
`SelectPreferredCameraChildFromRouteEntity(route, 0)` and checks the child vtable ==
`CameraControlStrafe` (off_143054560 = the aim/strafe camera). So each player fires
along the aim camera of ITS screen index.

- Local player (screen 0) → screen-0 aim camera = the rendered viewport camera
  (CameraManager(0), which the sender reads at +0x1B0 = kCameraRotationOffset).
- Co-op Second player (screen index 1 at Player+0x4010) → screen-1 aim camera,
  which the mod NEVER drives.

**Why the current mod relay is insufficient:** `apply_peer_aim_facing_to_player`
relays `peer.camera_quat` but only blends its yaw into the Second player's BODY quat
(Player+0x140) via `camera_forward_horizontal`/`yaw_quat_from_horizontal_forward`.
The fire path ignores the body quat and reads the screen-1 aim camera, so the
Second player shoots wherever its uncontrolled screen-1 camera happens to point.
The `derive_look_stick_from_camera` path only feeds a RELATIVE right-stick delta,
which cannot reproduce an absolute aim direction.

**Secondary (convention) note:** `camera_forward_horizontal` uses the +Z basis
column (2(xz+wy), 1-2(x^2+y^2)); if the engine camera looks down -Z this yaw is
180-deg inverted, and `quat_horizontal_yaw` mixes pitch into the denominator
(m00 not m22) so it is only exact for yaw-only quats. Both are moot for the fix
below (a direct quat copy needs no derivation), but they are latent bugs in the
body-facing path.

**Fix direction (STATIC hypothesis, needs a runtime linkage check before build):**
drive the Second player's screen-1 aim camera rotation directly from the peer's
camera quaternion — copy peer CameraManager(0)+0x1B0 -> receiver
CameraManager(1)+0x1B0 (or the route-1 preferred-camera child's rotation). A DIRECT
quat copy is convention-agnostic (same field/frame on both copies) and sidesteps
the +Z/-Z derivation entirely. This is the previously-disabled "write CameraManager
on receiver" (apply_peer_gameplay_camera_for_player, left empty because it hijacked
the local viewport / sniper overlay / Nadine vanish) — BUT that disable was for
CameraManager(0), the RENDERED screen. CameraManager(1) is screen-1's camera and
should not hijack the rendered screen-0 viewport.

**Runtime linkage check required first (do not build blind):** while the Second
player aims, confirm that (a) GetCameraManager(1)+0x1B0 is the same rotation the
fire's `ResolveScreenRouteEntityByIndex(1)` path reads, and (b) writing
CameraManager(1)+0x1B0 does NOT alter the rendered screen-0 view. If CameraManager(1)
is not the route-1 camera, target the route-1 preferred-camera child from
SelectPreferredCameraChildFromRouteEntity instead. Status: **STATIC** (direction
source CONFIRMED in disasm; camera-write target is HYPOTHESIS pending runtime).

### Co-op aim direction, refined: fire reads a per-screen camera transform, NOT CameraManager+0x1B0 (STATIC, 2026-07-05)

Deeper trace of the direction source (correcting the prior turn's fix hypothesis).

**CONFIRMED — screen index == CameraManager index.** `ResolveScreenRouteEntityBy
Index` (`0x141C06420`) IS `CameraManager::Get(index)`: its own asserts read
`"index >= 0 && index < kNumScreens"` / `"CameraManager::Get"` / `"pMgr != NULL"`,
it indexes the two-entry table `0x14697AD50` (the camera-manager table:
slot0=(0x10E0200160,0x19), slot1=(0x10E0200188,0x1A)) and returns
`*(handle+8)` = the CameraManager for that screen. So the fire's
`CameraManager::Get(*(controllerOwner+0x4010))` picks the firing player's own
screen CameraManager (Second player screen index 1 -> CameraManager(1)).

**CONFIRMED — the fire's direction transform is a per-screen cache, not +0x1B0.**
The camera transform is produced by `sub_141C06650(cameraMgr, out)`
(CameraManager_GetBlendedCameraTransform): it selects the active camera child
(`SelectPreferredCameraChildFromRouteEntity` `0x141C0D4B0`, child list at mgr+0x100,
child mode at child+0x1B0=432 with strafe/aim = 3..4) and copies the transform from
either the per-screen cache `g_PerScreenCameraTransformCache` (`0x1465FDAA0`,
stride 0x400 = 64 xmmword per screen index `*(mgr+292)`) when a single camera is
active, or a blend built from `mgr+0x1A0`. It does NOT read `CameraManager+0x1B0`.

**REJECTED (refines the 2026-07-05 "wrong aim" entry):** the proposed fix "copy
peer CameraManager(0)+0x1B0 -> receiver CameraManager(1)+0x1B0" will NOT steer the
Second player's shot. `+0x1B0` on the manager is the sender-side readable current
rotation (what `capture_gameplay_camera_quat` samples and what drives the body-quat
relay), but the FIRE reads the per-screen transform cache `0x1465FDAA0[0x400*idx]` /
the blended child transform — a different field fed FROM the active camera child.

**Next lever candidates (for a build-ready fix):**
1. The active aim camera CHILD for screen 1 (the CameraControlStrafe object returned
   by SelectPreferredCameraChildFromRouteEntity on CameraManager(1)) — drive its
   own yaw/pitch orientation state from the peer camera each frame. Cleanest
   (authoritative, input-integrated), but needs the child's yaw/pitch offsets.
2. `g_PerScreenCameraTransformCache 0x1465FDAA0 + 0x400*1` (screen-1 entry) — write
   the peer transform here each frame AFTER the camera update. Simpler target but
   it is a cache refreshed from the child, so timing (post-update override) matters
   and it has many writers/readers.

Next static step: RE the CameraControlStrafe child orientation state (yaw/pitch or
quat offsets) so option 1 can be written precisely; and identify the single
authoritative writer of `0x1465FDAA0[0x400*idx]` to know whether an option-2
override survives the frame. Status: **STATIC** (source CONFIRMED; write target
still HYPOTHESIS).

### Camera transform layout: matrix at cache_entry+0x350; buildable aim fix via GetBlendedCameraTransform hook (STATIC, 2026-07-05)

**Camera transform layout CONFIRMED.** `CameraManager_GetBlendedCameraTransform`
(`0x141C06650`) copies the chosen transform into its out buffer via
`sub_14014BDA0` (CameraState_CopyTransformAndParams), which copies a region starting
at **+0x350**: four xmmwords at +0x350/+0x360/+0x370/+0x380 = a **4x4 camera matrix**
(orientation 3x3 + translation), followed by camera params (fov etc.) from +0x390
(matching the earlier `[idx<<10 + 0x1465FDAA0 + 0x390/+0x3A4]` reads). So
`g_PerScreenCameraTransformCache[0x400*idx] + 0x350` is the screen's camera matrix;
its upper 3x3 is the aim/shot direction basis the fire consumes.

   convention-agnostic if we build the matrix in the engine's basis.
2. Override `g_PerScreenCameraTransformCache[0x400*1] + 0x350` rotation each frame

**Runtime verification still required before build** (do not guess): confirm

### FIRE RAY SOURCE FOUND: per-screen camera pose seed at CameraManager+0xB0 -> +0x60 (STATIC, 2026-07-05)

**The fire direction chain is now closed end-to-end.**

1. `PlayerFireController_Fire(FireArgs&)` receives the aim ray inside FireArgs —
   both camera resolves INSIDE Fire are unrelated (line ~667 `Get(0)` = the shot
   NOISE/NPC-alert broadcast: faction bytes +496, distance vrsqrt; line ~999
   strafe-camera check = the `unzoomed-sniper-shots` stat counter).
2. FireArgs are built by the sole Fire caller `sub_140E2BCD0`
   (PlayerFireController_BuildFireArgsAndFire): it seeds the aim ray via
   `ResolveScreenRoutePoseSeedOrDefault(&seed, *(controllerOwner+0x4010))`
   (line 213) and cooks it through `sub_140CADD60` into FireArgs (v135) →
   `PlayerFireController_Fire`.
3. `ResolveScreenRoutePoseSeedOrDefault` (`0x141C077B0`) is
   `CameraManager::GetHandle(idx)` semantics: mgr = `0x14697AD50[idx]`;
   `blk = *(mgr+0xB0)`; requires gate bytes `blk+85` && `blk+86` and a bit test of
   `dword_14697AE34` inside the bitset at `*(blk+8)+32`; then the **pose seed =
   32 bytes at `blk+0x60` = [position float4][orientation quat float4]**.
   On any gate failure it returns the default **pos(0,0,0) + identity quat
   (xmmword_1428805D0 = 0,0,0,1)**.

**Root cause of "Second player shoots the wrong way": CONFIRMED (static).** The
Second player's screen-1 camera block either fails the gates (→ fires along the
IDENTITY direction from origin-ish seed) or holds an unmanaged stale pose. The mod
never writes screen-1's pose seed.

**Build-ready fix (two options, pick 1 first):**
1. **Hook `ResolveScreenRoutePoseSeedOrDefault` (0x141C077B0):** when `a2 == 1`
   (Second player screen) and the peer is aiming, write the out buffer directly:
   `out[0..15] = peer camera position, out[16..31] = peer.camera_quat`, return.
   No engine state touched, no gate hassle, single interception exactly where the
   fire ray is born.
2. Write `*(CameraManager(1)+0xB0)+0x60` each frame + satisfy gates +85/+86 and
   the `dword_14697AE34` bitset — heavier, engine-state-dependent.

**Protocol addition needed:** StatePacket carries `camera_quat` but NOT the camera
POSITION (the seed's first 16 bytes = ray origin). Cleanest: the SENDER reads its
own screen-0 seed verbatim (`*(CameraManager(0)+0xB0)+0x60`, 32 bytes) and relays
it; the receiver feeds those exact 32 bytes for screen 1. Same format both sides,
zero conversion, convention-proof. (Fallback if seed unreadable: player position +
eye-height offset + camera_quat.)

**Falsifiable prediction:** with the relay + hook, the Second player's shots land
where the peer's crosshair points (both copies), including while strafing; without
peer-aim the resolver behaves natively. Status: **STATIC** (chain CONFIRMED in
disasm; fix design build-ready, pending implementation + runtime test).

### Grenade THROW ANIMATION sync: native-trigger design, no separate anim relay (STATIC, 2026-07-05)

**Question:** does syncing grenades require relaying the throw animation itself?

**Answer (STATIC): no — the animation must come natively, like aim pose and fire
recoil.** The grenade throw animation (`s_standing-grenade-toss[-ap]`,
`cover-grenade-toss` family) is an ACTION on the player's own action graph. The
string users `sub_1405AE8E0`/`sub_1405AEAA0` are script action-name registrars; the
runtime trigger is the grenade controller committing the toss, which starts the
action on the throwing player's graph. The Second player is a full Player with its
own graph: when its OWN grenade controller processes hold→release (button relay)
it enters `GrenadeMove` (grenade-aim move-set, draw anim), shows the arc, and the
toss commit plays the throw animation — all natively per copy. This is the same
principle already proven by aim pose (sustained 0x200 → ADS stance) and fire
(button pulse → recoil anim): deliver the INPUT, not the animation.

**Cluster corrected/completed:**
- `0x140E17AC0` = PlayerGrenadeController_ResolveContextSettingsAndPose (settings
  id per movement context + pose seeds; called with 'Grenade Settings: %s' debug
  print) — label refined from the earlier UpdateAimArcAndToss guess.
- `0x140E1B000` = PlayerGrenadeController_SolveTrajectory (ballistic arc solve
  from settings gravity/speed at +0x18/+0x1C/+0x20; cached at this+0x3D0). Its six
  callers (0x140E19600, 0x140E1F440, 0x140E1F5B0, 0x140E1FB50, 0x140E23920,
  0x140E24A00) are the arc-preview and toss-commit paths — the toss commit among
  them is where the throw action/animation is requested (next static target if the
  native trigger stalls).

**Implication for the sync plan (unchanged, now covering animation):** grenade
hold/release button relay + pose-seed hook + grenade ammo on the Second player =
direction, projectile AND animation together. If runtime shows the toss action
being swallowed despite the button reaching the joypad, inspect the toss-commit
callers above and CheckActionExclusions (0x140E2ADF0). Status: **STATIC**.

### Effects sync (muzzle/tracers/impacts/explosions): native per-copy consequences, no relay layer needed (STATIC, 2026-07-05)

**Design question:** do bullet tracers/impact decals/muzzle flashes and explosions
need their own sync channel?

**Answer: no — they are side-effects of REAL native projectiles in each copy.**
1. **Bullets.** The receiving copy delivers the peer's shot by pulsing the Second
   player's own fire button → its PlayerFireController fires a REAL
   `ProjectileBulletInstant`. Runtime evidence already on file: the 2026-07-04
   receiver crash happened INSIDE `ProjectileBulletInstant::ProbeKick`
   (`sub_14152C9B0`, rva 0x152CB38) on a relayed shot — proof that relayed shots
   run the full native projectile pipeline on the receiver, which is exactly the
   pipeline that draws muzzle flash, tracer and impact/decal effects. Per-weapon
   toggles exist (`allow-tracer`, `no-tracers`, `ParticleMuzzleFlashTint`,
   `bullet-impacts`). Once the pose-seed fix lands, those effects follow the
   CORRECT direction automatically.
2. **Explosions.** `ProcessExplosion` (game/process-explosion.cpp: `Init`
   `sub_1402E6E10` 0x90C, `Active::Update`, `ApplyDamageToObject`,
   `spawn-explosion-effects-locator`) is a process spawned by the detonating
   projectile — no direct Init callers (virtual process-system spawn). The Second
   player's natively thrown grenade detonates per copy → native explosion visuals
   there. Debug lever `Control Grenade Explosions Manually` exists for testing.
3. **What can diverge (accepted for now):** per-copy RNG spread → impact points
   differ slightly; grenade trajectories can diverge if local collisions differ →
   explosion position/timing mismatch. Fallback if runtime shows it matters:
   relay a compact ExplosionEvent (position + art id) and spawn via the process
   system — deep, only if needed. Enemy damage consistency is the ENEMY-sync
   phase's concern (host-authoritative), not an effects problem.

**Conclusion:** the effects "sync" task collapses into the already-planned work:
(a) pose-seed relay + hook (direction), (b) grenade trigger + ammo (real grenade),
(c) keep native fire via button pulse. No separate effects channel. Status:
**STATIC** (bullet pipeline point is backed by prior runtime crash evidence).

### Reliable-events map: button-driven actions relay for free; only side-effects need work (STATIC, 2026-07-05)

**Command resolution chain CONFIRMED end-to-end.** Authored player commands are
NOT fixed bits — `Joypad_IsCommandActive(joypad, cmdHash, edge)` (0x141837CD0)
resolves up to two binding descriptors and evaluates each via
`Joypad_EvaluateCommandDescriptor` (0x141838050: analog threshold + digital button +
hold timing + dependencies + temp disables), whose digital path is
`Joypad_EvaluateGamepadButtonBinding` (0x141838C90) — which reads the **Joypad
pressed/released/current masks at +0xD0/+0xD8/+0xE0 and per-button timestamps at
+0x10C**. Those are exactly the masks the engine derives (via Input_ScaleCopyVirtual)
from the resolved input block +0x518 that the co-op mod already relays.

**Consequence:** every button/analog-mapped action resolves from the SAME relayed
Joypad state, so it fires natively on the Second player's own graph (input, then
native action + native animation per copy). The mod strips only scope layer bits
(0x10000..0x80000) and fire (0x800, delivered via FirePacket); everything else in
block+0x518 passes through the ScaleCopy sandwich.

**Reliable-events triage:**
- COME FREE (input relay only): jump, dodge/roll, crouch, sprint, cover, vault/
  interact BUTTON, melee BUTTON, reload BUTTON, weapon-switch BUTTON, grenade
  hold/release. No per-action code.
- NEED A CONSISTENT SIDE-EFFECT (already-planned phases, not new channels):
  * weapon switch / reload: WHICH weapon + ammo — covered by the held-weapon relay
    (held_weapon_art_id + gun_state) and pre-give; ammo is cosmetic per-copy.
  * aim/fire/grenade DIRECTION: the pose-seed relay+hook (v8) already planned.
  * melee / interact / vault: TARGET/CONTEXT-dependent (an enemy, a ledge, a
    door). Needs the target present at the same spot -> falls under position sync
    (done for players) + the ENEMY-sync phase (melee target) + scripted-interact
    context (may no-op on the receiver; accept or relay an InteractEvent later).

**Correction to the 2026-07-05 grenade note:** `PlayerFireController_CheckAction
Exclusions` (0x140E2ADF0) is a FIRE suppressor — it blocks the GUN from firing
while an authored Grenade/Grenade-Add/Grapple/Grapple-Add/gun-up-layer action is
active. It does NOT gate the grenade throw itself, so it is not a grenade-sync
blocker (it correctly prevents a shot mid-throw). Removed from the grenade
open-items list.

Status: **STATIC** — command relay coverage CONFIRMED in disasm; the remaining
work is entirely the already-scoped weapon/position/enemy phases, not per-event
channels.

### Melee target is LOCAL (combat controller field), folds into enemy-sync (STATIC, 2026-07-05)

**Melee target selection is not networked per player.** The `get-player-melee-target`
script handler (`sub_141213C40`) reads it as: local player handle
`g_PlayerHandleForHudPublish` -> `player+0x1F60` (combat/melee controller) ->
virtual +0x1C8 -> result `+0xD8` = the current melee TARGET entity id. The target
is chosen locally by `melee-attack-rater.cpp` (rater `sub_1411F7370`, 0x1861,
shared by player + NPC melee behaviors) rating nearby enemies by geometry; it is a
locally-maintained field, not a relayed value.

**Co-op consequence (confirms the reliable-events triage):** the Second player's
melee button relays for free -> its OWN melee controller selects a target from ITS
local enemy set -> plays the melee action on it. Correct behavior therefore
requires the enemies to be POSITION-SYNCED (the enemy-sync phase): with matched
enemy positions the local rating picks the same target the peer hit. No melee
event channel is needed for the input/animation.

**Documented fallback (only if enemy-sync proves insufficient for melee):** relay
the peer's chosen target id (readable at peer `player+0x1F60 -> +0x1C8 -> +0xD8`)
and, on the receiver, bias the Second player's target to the matching synced enemy.
Deferred — enemy position sync should make local selection converge on its own.

Note: the `get-player-melee-target` query is hardwired to the LOCAL player handle,
so it is a HUD/script convenience, NOT the path the Second player's melee execution
uses (that goes through the Second player's own combat controller directly).
Status: **STATIC** — melee target locality CONFIRMED; folds into enemy-sync, no new
channel.
