### 2026-07-09: pose-only FirePacket button fallback restored after aim-writer rejection

After the `SecondAimAtPos` crash, the crash log order separated two changes from
`26fc4e8`: both copies logged `SECOND-AIM-AT-POS ...` before any
`FIRE-RELAY button ...`, so the aim writer was the failing path. The FirePacket
button fallback is restored independently: pose-only no longer drains packets with
`FIRE-RELAY skip: pose-only`; it falls through to the existing one-shot
`kJoypadFireButtonMask` path. Native `PlayerFireController::Fire` replay remains
gated by full puppet ADS (`g_puppet_relay_aim_press` / F8) because unaimed native
replay previously crashed one tick later.

Runtime prediction for this narrower fix: peer shots should log `FIRE-RELAY button`
again, while no `SECOND-AIM-AT-POS` writer exists in code and no `AIM-TARGET-WRITE`
path is enabled by default.

### 2026-07-09: FirePacket fallback was still gated by F8 inside Input_ScaleCopy

**CONFIRMED by code inspection after user runtime:** restoring the FirePacket queue
was insufficient because the actual Joypad3 feed in `hooked_input_scale_copy`
only ORed `kJoypadFireButtonMask` into `source+0x518` inside
`if (g_puppet_relay_aim_press)`. Since F8/full puppet ADS is OFF by default, the
button fallback could be queued but never reach the puppet input conversion.

**Fix:** fire pulse `0x800` is now independent of aim-press relay. Aim `0x200`
remains gated separately. FirePacket sending is also symmetric now; role B no
longer returns before `sendto`, so either copy can publish shots.

**Aim animation guard:** the old default-on aim relay is still rejected for
running/turning. The replacement default is narrower: auto `0x200` only for
non-scoped peer aim while the peer is almost stationary (`move_magnitude <= 0.08`
and low horizontal velocity). Scoped ADS and moving aim still require explicit F8
or a future native aim-additive path.

### 2026-07-09: wrong/static aim direction traced to sender seed source + stale F8 gate

**Runtime symptom:** shots now relay, but both shots and visible aim point in the
wrong direction; rotating the local camera leaves the remote puppet aiming at a
static point.

**Static/code root cause:** the sender still packed `pose_seed` through
`GetCameraManager(0)+0xB0+0x60`, while the confirmed resolver source is the
route-table chain `table_14697AD50[0] -> +8 -> +0xB0 -> +0x60`. Prior findings
already showed `GetCameraManager` and the route table are different chains. Also,
the new stationary auto-aim press enabled Joypad `0x200`, but the caller-scoped
pose-seed override (`0x10E934B` / `0xCB17D6`) was still gated by manual F8 only,
so visible aim could keep using the puppet's stale native screen-1 camera.

**Fix:** `copy_local_pose_seed_32` now reads the route-table idx-0 source, sender
uses that same 32-byte seed for both `StatePacket.pose_seed` and `camera_quat`, and
the caller-scoped receiver override is enabled by the movement-aware
`puppet_aim_press_relay_enabled_for_peer` helper. This does not re-enable the broad
screen-1 source write.

**Build/runtime harness:** release build passed; two copies were injected
(PID 20748 / 4040). Startup logs show `PlayerFireController::Fire capture installed`
for both and no rejected `SECOND-AIM-AT-POS` / broad `AIM-TARGET-WRITE` path in the
idle tail. The falsifiable runtime signal for the actual fix is
`POSE-SEED-SEND route0 q=(...)` while the local player holds strict aim/RMB, followed
by peer aim/fire direction tracking camera turns instead of a static point.

### 2026-07-09: rifle/static aim follow-up — split pose relay from ADS press

**Runtime symptom:** after switching to the route-table sender seed, packets showed
changing `POSE-SEED-SEND route0 q=(...)`, but the receiver still aimed/fired at a
wrong/static direction. Rifle aim could also make the puppet disappear for a couple
of seconds.

**Static/code correction:** `puppet_aim_press_relay_enabled_for_peer` intentionally
returns false for rifle/scoped peer aim unless F8 is enabled, because relaying puppet
ADS/`0x200` is the path that leaks scoped HUD/DrawControl state. Reusing that helper
for caller-scoped pose-seed override accidentally disabled the safe direction relay
for rifle aim too. Split the gates: ADS press still uses the scoped-rifle guard, but
pose-seed/camera-basis relay uses `puppet_aim_pose_relay_enabled_for_peer`, which is
caller-scoped and does not inject `0x200`. `AIM-POSE-OVERRIDE` is force-logged so the
runtime test can distinguish "seed sent" from "receiver actually substituted it".

**Runtime symptom:** aiming the sniper still made the second player disappear on the

the local player's own sniper scope is not suppressed.

### 2026-07-10: phantom ADS source confirmed - Player ADS field is not strict input

**Runtime evidence:** while neither copy was being aimed, both PIDs continuously
logged `POSE-SEED-SEND` and the receiver continuously logged
`AIM-POSE-OVERRIDE`. At the same time the remote drive log showed `btn=0x0` for
almost every frame. Therefore the sender's `local_player_strict_aim_active` gate
was true without a physical aim command.

**Cause / correction:** the gate accepted `player_ads_active(player)` before
checking RMB. That field is an animation/weapon-state output and can remain true
during weapon draw or transition states; it is not proof of current player intent.
For the two-instance PC path, strict aim now means physical RMB while this process's
game window is foreground. Sender logs `STRICT-AIM-SEND ON/OFF` on transitions.
This makes packet `0x200`, peer camera, and pose seed clear immediately on RMB
release instead of latching phantom ADS.

removed/replaced slot 1 and entered the same puppet `GiveWeapon` through delayed
slot mirroring.

**Correction:** Type-97 is now rejected by the central puppet-give allow check,
hard-blocked inside `safe_give_weapon_art_to_puppet`, and marked ungivable by
`SLOT-MIRROR` before the current slot is removed. Its real `WeaponInfo` packet is
still stored for static analysis. M30 and all previously safe pickup arts retain
their existing relay path; when the peer replaces M30 with Type-97, the receiver
keeps M30 visible rather than entering the known hang.

### 2026-07-10: pickup immediate-apply race confirmed; Type-97 ammo=-1 hypothesis

**M30 freeze sequence:** receiver logged `GIVEWEAPON-RELAY-APPLY ... ok=1` and
`PUPPET-AFTER-GIVE ... s1=0x3019cbee`, proving M30 was created successfully. In the
same game-thread pass, `SLOT-MIRROR` still consumed the older peer snapshot with
pistol in slot 1, removed M30, and re-gave the pistol. This mixes two inventory
owners and explains the freeze/fight when replacing Nadine's sniper. Correction:
all `WeaponGivePacket`s now store the real block only; debounced `SLOT-MIRROR` is
the sole remove+give owner.

**Type-97 static difference:** among fields actually consumed by decompiled
`PlayerWeaponController::GiveWeapon`, Type-97 carries `WeaponInfo+0x84 = -1`, while
working M30 carries `37`. The `-1` value enters a separate default/random-ammo path
through the online weapon definition. The two observed Type-97 hangs both used the
raw `-1` block. New falsifiable hypothesis: retain the exact Type-97 art/model but
normalize only the stored puppet copy's ammo to finite value `1`, then let stable
slot mirroring perform the one swap. `TYPE97-INFO-NORMALIZE` distinguishes this
path in the runtime log.

### 2026-07-10: sender-side M30 freeze = false pickup-id self-apply

**Runtime proof:** exact Type-97 display succeeded with normalized ammo:
`TYPE97-INFO-NORMALIZE`, then `SLOT-MIRROR ... art=0x27617d0d ... gave=1`. On the
same local copy, the subsequent M30 pickup completed native `GiveWeapon`, sent the
relay packet, and logged `SENDER-AFTER-PICKUP ... s1=0x3019cbee`; the receiver also
logged `GIVEWEAPON-RELAY-STORED`. The sender then stopped before its expected
`PICKUP-APPLY` tail and spun, proving the hang was after successful local pickup and
outside receiver inventory mirroring.

**Cause / correction:** `weapon_info_pickup_consume_fields` treated
`WeaponInfo+0x58` as a runtime pickup id and called `NetEventSyncWeaponPickups::Apply`
again on the sender. Both Type-97 and M30 carried the identical value `0xE446A2CE`,
so it cannot identify their distinct world objects. Type-97 happened to return
`ok=0`; M30 entered a non-returning native path. The GiveWeapon-tail no longer
self-applies or transmits a `PickupPacket` derived from this false id. Exact weapon
display remains owned by `WeaponGivePacket` plus stable `SLOT-MIRROR`.

### 2026-07-10: repeated pickup display lag/staleness = lifetime dedup plus destructive store

**Runtime proof:** after M30/AUG/Type-97 switching, the second local Type-97 pickup
completed `GIVEWEAPON-CALL art=0x27617d0d` and the raw snapshot changed to Type-97,
but there was no second `GIVEWEAPON-RELAY-SEND`. The receiver therefore logged
`SLOT-MIRROR-SKIP ... art=0x27617d0d keep=0xc3181ebd` and retained the previous
weapon. This matches the sender's session-lifetime art dedup: each pickup art was
transmitted only once per injected process.

**Additional delay causes:** every received pickup block cleared the whole
four-entry relay store before writing element zero, so only the newest art was
re-givable. When a raw `StatePacket` arrived before its matching give packet, the
ungivable branch also wrote the normal five-second apply memo, delaying use of the
block even after it arrived.

**Correction:** every native pickup `GiveWeapon` event now sends its captured
block, the receiver retains up to eight distinct pickup blocks (refreshing by art
and replacing round-robin only when full), and an ungivable raw slot no longer
starts the five-second cooldown. The existing one-second stable-snapshot debounce
remains the sole intentional delay before a non-empty puppet inventory swap.

### STATIC 2026-07-10: pickup animation starts at RequestInteract, before inventory give

The player interaction graph closes the pickup-action boundary:

- `WeaponPickup` vtable `+0x248` (`0x1408A9AA0`) returns the object's interact
  control at `WeaponPickup+0x510`.
- `WeaponPickupInteractControl` vtable `+0x28` is `0x1408C8A40`, confirmed by its
  own `PickupInteractControl::RequestInteract` assert in `process-pickup.cpp`. It
  publishes `interact-with-me` for the pickup and player.
- `Player_InteractDispatcher` calls that virtual at `0x140C875B3`, then immediately
  calls `0x140C87D70`, which publishes the separate player-side
  `player-requested-interact` state. The authored command ids
  `weapon-pickup-swap` / `weapon-pickup-when-no-weapon` are selected upstream by
  `Player_ResolveWeaponPickupInteractAnim` (`0x140C7FF40`).
- The eventual inventory mutation is separate: local ground pickup later reaches
  the script `give-weapon` branch (`0xFB1091A3`, return `0x140DD4208`). Therefore a
  receiver can reproduce only `player-requested-interact` and leave inventory to
  the already stable `WeaponGivePacket + SLOT-MIRROR` path.

`Player_PublishRequestedInteract` resolves its target actor from thread-local
state (`FlsGetValue(...)[19]`), not from an explicit player argument. The replay
must therefore run inside the retained puppet's per-player update; calling it from
the global drive tick risks animating Chloe. Runtime prediction: a local weapon
pickup logs `PICKUP-ANIM-SEND`, the peer resolves the same `WeaponPickup` runtime
id/art and logs `PICKUP-ANIM-APPLY ... resolved=1 ok=1` before the later
`GIVEWEAPON-RELAY-STORED`. The puppet should bend once, while any replay-generated
`OnInteract` or `give-weapon` completion is suppressed and cannot mutate inventory.

The remaining weapon display debounce is changed independently from one second on
the full 32-byte snapshot to 500 ms per mirrored slot. Unrelated holster/gadget
slot changes can no longer restart the picked weapon's timer; empty initial slots
still fill immediately.

### 2026-07-10 (STATIC, ПРОРЫВ): рецепт pickup-жеста + обход блокера +0x518

Два решающих факта убивают «естественный» путь для куклы:
1. Player_InteractDispatcher (0x140C85D20) пролог = `mov rax,rsp; ...; lea rbp,[rax-0xD38]`
   (frame-from-entry-rsp) → call-трамплайн крашит (как reticle-функция).
2. Диспетчер проверяет команды по PER-SCREEN списку block+0x590 (InputScreenBlock_
   IsCommandActive 0x14183A3D0), НЕ по +0x518 → релеенные кнопки куклы НЕ триггерят
   интеракт (подтверждает, почему кукла не подбирает сама).

РЕЦЕПТ из диспетчера (ветка старта pickup-анимации, decompile line ~1651):
- `Player_ResolveWeaponPickupInteractAnim(player, pickup, &a3, &a4, a5, &cmdId)`
  (0x140C7FF40) → выдаёт cmdId (a6) для weapon-pickup-swap/when-no-weapon.
- `sub_140C88130(player_side, cmdId, ...)` — publish.
- **`sub_14183A650(g_LocalPlayerInputManager+3504+3056*screenIdx, cmdId)`
  (0x14183A650, 0x314)** — АКТИВИРУЕТ команду в per-screen списке +0x590. Это
  парная к IsCommandActive и КЛЮЧ: активировать интеракт-команду НАПРЯМУЮ, минуя
  роутинг кнопок → родная anim-система куклы отыграет жест.
- `sub_141C9A360(interactControl, player, &stackStruct, 0)` (0x141C9A360, 0x159) —
  старт interact-действия.

per-screen block = `*(g_module+0x3FE1088=g_LocalPlayerInputManager) + 3504 +
3056*screenIdx`; screenIdx куклы = player+0x4010 (=1). ПЛАН: на кукле per-player
апдейте резолвить cmdId + вызвать sub_14183A650(puppetBlock, cmdId); если жеста нет
— добавить sub_141C9A360. Инвентарь НЕ трогать (give уже идёт через WeaponGivePacket);
следить, чтобы активация команды не запускала повторную выдачу.

### 2026-07-10: камера-блок (screen-0) live-diff — снова только ВЫХОДЫ, чистого pitch-входа нет

Дамп камера-блока blk=*(*(table_14697AD50[0]+8)+176), aim up vs down (тело неподвижно):

  питчем) — это ВЫХОД, что резолвер копирует в player+0x1720/+0x1730.

camera pose seed (blk+0x60) -> player+0x1720/+0x1730 -> рендер aim-позы + fire ray.

output, camera block) = ВЫХОД, пересчитывается каждый кадр. Истинный вход = aim-угол,
который стик интегрирует в aim-контроллере; писать его = driveить aim-стейт куклы,

### 2026-07-10 (RUNTIME REJECT): pickup bend is neither play-simple-gesture nor direct play-animation

Static analysis mapped the two reusable authored Player animation paths in
`Player_ScriptWeaponEventHandler 0x140DCDEA0`:

- CRC `0xC1F3F991` is `play-simple-gesture`. It resolves `<gesture>--part` and
  `<gesture>--add` against `Player+0x1A0` and calls
  `SsAnimateController::HandleEventAnimate 0x141E4FDD0`.
- CRC `0x09A3F435` is direct `play-animation`. Its single Event parameter is a
  pointer-backed, type-18, 264-byte `AnimateParams`; `0x14043DEB0 -> 0x141831310`
  resolves the pointer. `InitializeAnimateParams 0x141E45980` proves the payload
  is scalar/StringId/matrix POD; the actor handle is rebuilt separately.
- The retail handler prologue is trampoline-safe and begins with hidden neutral
  REX byte `0x40` before the seven pushes; runtime bytes matched the final 20-byte
  signature and the detour installed in both copies.

Two runtime builds then observed repeated real M-30 pickups. Every pickup logged
`GiveWeapon ret_rva=0xDD4208`, sent/received the weapon block, and completed
SLOT-MIRROR, but logged no `play-simple-gesture` and no `play-animation` on the
sender. Thus the visible local bend is generated outside both authored Player
event paths; relaying these events is **REJECTED** as a pickup-animation solution.
All experimental runtime code was removed after the falsifier. The evidence now
supports the foundational path: identify and activate the stock local-player-1
controller scheduler/ownership for the retained slot-1 Player instead of adding
another per-feature animation replay.

### 2026-07-10 (STATIC/RUNTIME): restore the real screen-1 interact tick; direct action pending

The `PlayerWeaponController_GiveWeapon -> 0x1413B49B0` path initially looked like
the missing pickup-animation queue. It is not. `0x1413B2340` constructs a 0x368-byte
`Hud` per screen, binds `Hud+0x320` to a static 0x19A0-byte state block, and
`0x1413B2730` initializes both screen 0 and screen 1. The list at nested `+0x1890`
(count `+0x1930`, cap 5) is therefore a HUD pickup-notification list. The stock
`0x1413538B0` frame wrapper updates only screen 0 through `0x1413B2950`, but adding
the missing screen-1 Hud tick cannot own the character's bend and was removed from
the active source.

The actual Player interaction boundary requires more than activating a command:

- `Player_BuildInteractDispatchState` `0x140C805A0` builds 0x15C bytes from
  `(screenIndex, player transform)`, resolves `g_PlayerHandleForHudPublish[index]`,
  copies `*interact-command-list*`, and snapshots per-screen `+0x590` command state.
- `Player_InteractDispatcher` `0x140C85D20` consumes that state and the indexed
  dispatcher at `0x143EC4EE0 + 0x35C0*screenIndex`.
- Its pickup branch obtains the pickup's interact control, activates the resolved
  command, builds a 16-byte retained Player handle from `Player+0xA8/+0xBC`, and
  calls `Player_StartInteractAction` `0x141C9A360`.
- `Player_StartInteractAction` immediately calls interact-control vtable `+0x8`
  with `(control, interactable, playerHandle)`; a return of `-1` rejects the action.

Runtime after restoring `BuildInteractDispatchState -> Player_InteractDispatcher`
for screen 1 showed `PICKUP-GESTURE ... ok=1 dispatch=0` on the relayed M-30 event.
Thus the previous no-animation result was not only a missing tick: the full native
dispatcher still selected no eligible nearby interaction.

**HYPOTHESIS, current build:** while the 700 ms gesture window is armed, inspect the
screen-1 dispatcher's already-native nearby list for a `WeaponPickup` whose art
matches the relayed `WeaponGivePacket`, then call `Player_StartInteractAction` once.
The existing 2.5 s suppression prevents receiver-side `OnInteract` and scripted
GiveWeapon completion from mutating inventory; SLOT-MIRROR remains authoritative.
Prediction: `PICKUP-GESTURE direct-start ... result!=-1` and a visible puppet bend.
No matching nearby object, `result=-1`, or an accepted action without a bend will
separately falsify object selection, action acceptance, or downstream animation.

Per-screen blob `0x143EC4EE0 + 0x35C0*screenIndex`: count@+0, 32-byte entries@+8,

### 2026-07-10 CORRECTION: Exp 2/3 Player-scheduler classification is REJECTED

The runtime observation `spot_count=1` is valid, but its proposed connection to
the missing Player update is false.

1. `0x1403E84F0` is `NpcManager_RegisterSpotActor`; `0x1403E3E30` consumes that
   list through source-identified `Npc::UpdatePathSearch(void)` `0x14043B830`.
   The list is an NPC spot/path-search list, not the canonical local Player list.
2. RTTI resolves `0x14042FCF0` as vtable `+0x410` for `Npc`, `Buddy`, and `Human`.
   `0x1404901B0` is the Alcazar override of that same slot. Player vtable
   `0x142A4BFE8 + 0x410` instead points to `Player_Update` `0x1410EC230`.
3. RTTI resolves `0x14042D120`, previously named `Player_AnimPhaseOwnerUpdate`, as
   `Active@Npc` vtable `+0x20` (`0x142934888`). The related `421150 -> 422760`
   control-host chain is therefore NPC-side and must not be promoted on a Player.
4. Exp2's `42FCF0(puppet)` fault is explained by calling the wrong class virtual
   implementation on a Player object. It does not prove missing scheduler TLS or
   frame ordering. Both that drive and the forced `player+0x15A9 bit1` write are
   removed from the hook after their REJECTED results.
5. `Player+0x1A0` is not established as an anim instance. Existing static work
   maps it as the upper Player state owner built/published through Player vtable
   `+0x700/+0x710`; non-null `+0x1A0` cannot prove animation-job registration.

### Player vtable+0x410 is dispatched by the animation manager (STATIC)

`AnimManager_AsyncObjectUpdateJointBlendJob` `0x141A92A00` carries the source
path/function identity from `anim-mgr-jobs.cpp`. It resolves a retained owner from
the job record at `+0x1A8/+0x1B0`; when job flags contain `0x20`, it calls owner
vtable `+0x410`, then `+0x418`. The companion dispatcher `0x141A8F9D0` maps phase
bits `8/0x10/0x20` to vtable `+0x400/+0x408/+0x410` respectively.

For Player RTTI this reaches `Player_Update` `0x1410EC230`. This is the first
statically supported scheduling path relevant to the missing pickup animation.
The remaining alternatives are: no animation job for the puppet; a job without
phase bit `0x20`; a retained pair resolving another owner; or a later rejection in
the upper Player action/overlay pipeline. Next work must trace animation-job
creation and flag writers before adding a read-only slot0/puppet comparison.

### 2026-07-10 Exp 5b (runtime, negative): interact path resists our hook techniques

Vtable-slot swap of `sub_140EC6C10` (thought to be PlayerInteractController update)
installed cleanly on both copies but logged ZERO `INTERACT-UPD-RUN` for slot0 OR

different path.

`Player_InteractDispatcher 0x140C85D20` (the convergence chokepoint, direct-called
from 4 sites) CANNOT be trampoline-hooked: live prologue is
`48 8B C4 (mov rax,rsp); push rbp/rsi/rdi/r12-15; 48 8D A8 C8 F2 FF FF
(lea rbp,[rax-0xD38])` = frame built from ENTRY rsp, the exact pattern that crashed
the GetTargetPointFromReticle trampoline (a call-detour shifts rsp by 8 ->
rbp misaligned -> crash). It is not virtual, so no vtable slot to swap either.

**Viable next technique (Exp 5c):** hook the CALL SITES, not the function entry.
Patch the `call Player_InteractDispatcher` instruction at each of its 4 callers
(0x140C8829B built-state, 0x140CD4526 scripted, 0x140D74893, 0x140EC7CBA revive)
to call a thunk that logs the player arg (rcx/r8 per site) then jumps to the real
target - entering with the caller's correct rsp, so no frame issue. Alternatively
find a trampoline-SAFE (push-based prologue) function uniquely on the interact
per-frame path. This tells us whether interact dispatch runs for the puppet.

The vtable-swap probe code is retained (harmless: the swapped slot is never
dispatched) but should be repointed or removed next turn. Baseline stable.

### 2026-07-10 GRENADE SYNC — native path mapped (feature outside the puppet-controller wall)

Grenades are a WORLD-OBJECT (ProjectileGrenade NdGameObject), not a puppet-controller
action - so throw/flight/explosion sync is feasible like enemy/fire relay (the throw
ANIMATION on the puppet remains the same authored-action wall; cosmetic).

Native functions (net-event-weapon.cpp / projectile-grenade):
- `ProjectileGrenade::Init` = `sub_141533560(grenade, a2, a3)` - fires on every grenade
  spawn/throw. Throw-path callers: `sub_14153FB90`, `sub_141540D60`.
- `EmitGrenadeProjectile` = `sub_14154B3B0(int,int,transform*,int,char,int,char,+stackf)`
  - the native SPAWN: reads a3=transform (position+dir), builds orientation via cross
  products. RECEIVER entry: call this with relayed params to spawn a real grenade
  that flies+explodes natively.
- `SendNetEventEmitGrenade` = `sub_140BE7000(ProjectileGrenade*, StringId, bool)` -
  MP send wrapper, gated by HIBYTE(g_NetModeFlags); its receive counterpart is the
  NetEventEmitGrenade class (vtable 0x1429DCCE0, RTTI 0x143761BC0).
- `SendNetEventGrenadeStartFuse(ProjectileGrenade*, float, StringId, float)` - fuse
  start relay (for detonation timing sync).
- Explosion: process-explosion.cpp; `GameArmor::ComputeExplosionDamage 0x140294610`;
  `suppress-grenade-explosions` / `Control Grenade Explosions Manually` script gates.

**Design (mirrors pickup relay that worked):**
1. SENDER: hook `ProjectileGrenade::Init 0x141533560` (fires on local throw) ->
   capture grenade type (StringId), spawn world transform (pos+dir), initial velocity,
   fuse -> relay UDP (new GrenadePacket).
2. RECEIVER: call `EmitGrenadeProjectile 0x14154B3B0` (or Init) on the game thread with
   reconstructed args -> spawns a matching grenade; native physics fly+explode it.
3. Double-damage: apply explosion damage on ONE side only (authoritative thrower), or
   spawn the peer grenade as cosmetic (suppress its damage) - decide after step 1.

### 2026-07-11 GRENADE SYNC — receiver spawn is the hard sub-problem (ABI is throw-math-derived)

EmitGrenadeProjectile `0x14154B3B0` has ONE caller, the throw action `sub_14040CEF0`

thrower). DIRECT ARG CONSTRUCTION IS NOT VIABLE - reproducing the args = reproducing
sub_14040CEF0. (Saves the next agent from trying.)

   and relays them; receiver calls sub_14154B3B0 with the relayed bytes + local
   thrower=puppet. Pro: args are VALID (from a real throw). Con: needs a raw
   machine-code thunk (MSVC x64 has no __declspec(naked)) - fragile, crash-prone.

   gameplay-critical part (damage/shake/effect); loses only the cosmetic arc. Still
   needs an explosion-trigger ABI but that path is already partly reversed (AttackInfo).

**Confirmed working today:** flight capture (pos@0x240, vel@0x260, quat@0x140 one
frame after Init hook). The blocker is purely the native spawn/detonate call ABI.
Throw ANIM stays walled. Probe (GRENADE-INIT/TRACK) retained; baseline stable.

### 2026-07-11 GRENADE/EXPLOSION SYNC — both blocked by the descriptor/process spawn system (honest ceiling)

`ProcessExplosion_Init 0x1402E7xxx` (game/process-explosion.cpp) is "Spawned via the
process system (no direct callers)" - explosions are instantiated by the process/
descriptor spawner with an explosion descriptor, not by a callable "explode at XYZ"
API. Same as EmitGrenadeProjectile: **every native world object (grenade projectile,
explosion process) is created through the descriptor/process spawn system with
per-object descriptors derived from complex state.** There is no cheap spawn API.

Consequence: grenade sync in ANY form (flight OR explosion-only) requires driving the
native descriptor/process spawner cross-process - the SAME hard sub-problem class as
materializing a real second player. It is a sub-project, not a quick win. The
`Spawn Test Explosions` debug menu exists but its item is in a menu data table (no
direct code xref to the string), so it did not yield a simple callable entry.

**Confirmed working (kept):** grenade FLIGHT CAPTURE on the sender (Init hook +
per-frame track: pos@0x240, vel@0x260, quat@0x140). The unsolved blocker is purely
the native SPAWN/DETONATE descriptor ABI on the receiver.

**Strategic note:** co-op features that REUSE/relay existing native state (enemy
transform match by name-hash, damage relay, existing-object sync) are tractable;
features that require SPAWNING new native world objects (grenades, explosions, real
2nd player) all hit the descriptor/process spawn wall. Prioritize the former.
Baseline + grenade probe stable, git clean.

### 2026-07-11 GRENADE ARC ROOT CAUSE: velocity is DERIVED from the event transform basis, not a writable field

Full static trace of the grenade spawn velocity path:
- EmitGrenadeProjectile `0x14154B3B0` computes projectileVelocity (`&v62`) from the
  launch transform via cross-product/basis math, passes it as arg4 (r9) to the spawn
  worker `sub_14154AAE0` ("IsFinite(projectileVelocity)", projectile-process.cpp),
  which bakes it into the ProcessSpawnInfo/descriptor.
- NetEventEmitGrenade::Execute `0x140BE63A0` ("Builds ProcessSpawnInfo, invokes the
  native descriptor materializer") RE-DERIVES the same velocity from the EVENT
  TRANSFORM (reads xmm11=[rax], xmm10=[rax+0x10] = the event+0x30 transform rows,
  cross-product math lines 223-257) plus a scalar at event+0x40 (=g+0x6F4). It then
  builds ProcessSpawnInfo (line 594) and spawns.

**Therefore the grenade's launch velocity is a SPAWN-DESCRIPTOR value derived from the
event transform basis - NOT a writable object field.** The current receiver machinery
(seh_write_grenade_launch_state writing +0x260/+0x270 + reapply_peer_grenade_arc
re-applying per frame + activation bytes) CANNOT create the arc: +0x260 is the
physics velocity OUTPUT (on the sender it only becomes valid at dt=63, one frame after
Init); the projectile integrates from its process/rigid-body state seeded at spawn,
which we never set. arcForced=1/fuse ok=1 report success but the grenade drops+detonates
at the spawn point because its spawn-seeded velocity is ~0.

**Correct fix (redirect):** make the EVENT carry the correct launch basis so Execute
derives the right velocity. The event transform (event+0x30, from Codex's
refresh_transform(g+0x100)) is captured at dt=63 = the FLIGHT transform, not the
throw-time launch basis. Either (a) capture the transform+scalar at throw time
(before the first physics frame consumes/changes them - hook the throw action
sub_14040CEF0 right after EmitGrenadeProjectile, or Init+the very next fields), or
(b) synthesize the event transform basis from the relayed launch velocity vector
(build an orthonormal basis whose forward = normalized velocity, scaled by |vel|) so
Execute's cross-product math reproduces it. Path (b) is self-contained and does not
depend on capture timing.

**Action for next turn:** REMOVE the +0x260 write / reapply_peer_grenade_arc dead-end;
implement path (b) - construct event+0x30 transform from the relayed vel + event+0x40
speed scalar, verify against Execute's exact basis convention. This is the real arc fix.

### 2026-07-11 GRENADE wall/ground clipping = the manual per-frame position teleport (confirms the redirect)

User report: peer grenade "falls through walls/ground constantly." Root: reapply_
peer_grenade_arc runs a MANUAL ballistic sim each frame (g_peer_arc_pos += vel*dt;
vel.y += kGrenadeGravityY) and FORCE-WRITES position via seh_write_grenade_launch_
state(..., set_position=true). Teleporting the object's transform every frame
bypasses collision -> clips through geometry; the manual gravity != engine gravity;
native physics/collision never run. This confirms the redirect: the mod must NOT
puppeteer the grenade frame-by-frame. Spawn ONCE with correct velocity seeded into
the process descriptor (event transform basis, path b) and let native physics fly +
collide it. REMOVE reapply_peer_grenade_arc + the set_position forcing entirely.

- heavy weapon: `0x140E858CE`, `call [PlayerAimController.vtable+0x58]`;
- ordinary weapon: `0x140E85925`, same slot;
- `rcx=PlayerAimController`, `rdx=targetPoint float4`, `r8=bodyForward float4`,
  `r9b=1`; stack arguments are native directional limits and a mode byte.

The target dataflow is complete:

1. At `0x140E853E3`, GunMoveShield calls PlayerAimController slot `+0xF8`, exact
   source-named method `PlayerAimController::GetTargetPointFromReticle
   0x140CB1720`.
2. At `0x140E853FF`, GunMoveShield slot `+0xF0` resolves to
   `GunMoveShield_CopyAimTargetPoint 0x140E84350`; the entire implementation is a
   16-byte copy, so no hidden conversion occurs.
3. At `0x140E858CE/0x140E85925`, that copied point is passed as slot `+0x58`'s
   first vector. The second vector is Player body-forward, derived from root
   orientation through `Quaternion_RotatePositiveZ 0x14014D9F0`.
4. Slot `+0x58` (`PlayerAimController_ApplyWorldAimBasis 0x140CAF110`) canonicalizes
   the two float4 vectors and calls slot `+0x50`.
5. Slot `+0x58` first calls controller slot `+0x80`,
   `PlayerAimController_GetAimOriginPoint 0x140CAFD90`. It selects `targHead` or
   `targPelvis` and resolves that skeleton joint's world position.
6. `PlayerAimController_ComputeDirectionalAimWeights 0x140CB32B0` begins with
   `normalize(targetPoint-internalAimOrigin)`, computes signed yaw/pitch relative to the
   Player body basis, clamps by directional limits, then calls
   `PlayerAimController_PublishDirectionalAimWeights 0x140CB41F0`.

`GetTargetPointFromReticle` itself resolves `Player+0x4010` through the screen-route
pose seed and constructs camera-origin plus camera-forward times ray distance. Thus
the static root cause of a fixed remote pose is the stale screen-1 target point, not
an inert anim graph. Since the downstream calculation normalizes target-origin, a
receiver hook can substitute `peerPosePosition + peerCameraForward*distance`; exact
distance is immaterial as long as it is finite and nonzero. Using the relayed pose
seed position mirrors the sender's native construction and avoids inventing a body
origin from the slot `+0x58` arguments.

The native limits should be preserved. Ordinary ADS supplies camera descriptor
fields `+0x74/+0x78` and two `60.0f` defaults (`0x142BE99FC`); the heavy-weapon
branch changes one limit to `-7.0f` (`0x142BEA1D8`). The single-screen byte is
`dword_143F051C8 <= 1` for ordinary ADS.

**Build-ready STATIC design:** vtable slot address `0x142A0B250` currently contains
`0x140CAF110`. Swap that slot, condition on owner `*(controller+0x108)` being the
slot-1 puppet plus a valid peer ADS pose seed, replace only the caller-owned target
float4 using peer quaternion `+Z`, and invoke the original with all native limits.
This avoids the rejected broad pose-seed, root-quaternion, downstream-field, and
frame-from-entry-rsp detour paths. No runtime test was performed.

**ABI/install guards (STATIC):** expected slot pointer is
`*(module+0x2A0B250) == module+0xCAF110`. Use a typed nine-argument function pointer;
raw disassembly proves stack arguments 5, 6, 8, and 9 are floats (`vmovss`), while
arguments 4 and 7 are bytes. The hook must pass through unless owner
`*(controller+0x108)` is retained Player slot 1 with `Player+0x4010 == 1` and a fresh
peer ADS pose seed. It should pass a hook-local target float4 rather than overwrite
the caller stack. All body-forward, mode, and limit arguments remain native. The
repository DLL has no `DLL_PROCESS_DETACH` restoration path, so install once and keep
the global slot swap for process lifetime.

### 2026-07-12 (static continuation): pickup-anim descriptor sink = the ACTOR's runtime state slot (validates context-replay)

Traced Player_PublishRequestedInteract 0x140C87D70 to its publish call:

`player-requested-interact` descriptor (class id from interactable+0x38, name id
from +0xD8, target actor from TLS ContextProcess) is dispatched into the target
ACTOR's per-actor runtime state slot - NOT a global HUD sink or a dispatcher-only
structure. It then sets a1+0x35B0 from g_LocalPlayerInputManager+80.

the anim graph consumes actor runtime state slots during that actor's Update, and
the puppet's Player_Update DOES run (Exp4 CONFIRMED FgAnimData ticks). So publishing
the descriptor with ContextProcess switched to the retained slot-1 puppet lands the
descriptor in the PUPPET's own state slot, which its own (running) anim graph reads
-> should bend the puppet for the pickup, without needing dispatcher promotion or a
mirrored WeaponPickup. This is the same class of mechanism as the aim-pose slot.

**Remaining runtime-only unknown:** whether the pickup-bend anim node keys on the
`player-requested-interact` slot ALONE (hyp 1) or also requires the world-side
`interact-with-me` event (hyp 2). The anim graph is data-driven; this last bit is
only decidable by the runtime test of the context-replay publish. The static quota
for implementing the candidate is now met (sink identified + puppet slot reachable +
puppet Update confirmed running).

### 2026-07-15 STATIC: production diagnostics caused avoidable hot-path load

The latest co session (PIDs 10800/2480) proved that Numpad7's unbalanced
`g_logging_enabled=true` left ordinary runtime logging active. In roughly the
interval represented by 242 half-second `PLAYER-INPUT-UPDATE` samples, the log
also accumulated sustained Joypad, movement, weapon, position, and cloth
telemetry; the shared file reached 17,149,302 bytes.

Source audit independently found per-conversion formatting in
`hooked_input_scale_copy`, diagnostic `GetCommand 0x14183ABF0` calls in the
Player input vtable hook, full DrawControl mesh/instance scans at the
NdAttachable post-joint callsite `0x141ED63F7`, and the completed spawn
experiment still arming DR0 on every game thread.

Build `2026-07-15cp` keeps functional relay ownership but compile-time parks
runtime logs and legacy Joypad probes, disables spawn DR0 capture, removes pure
GunMoveShield pass-through probes, and reduces cloth observation to a vtable and
parent identity heartbeat. Release build succeeds. Status: **STATIC /
HYPOTHESIS ready for runtime**, with prediction and competitors in
`reports/runtime_hot_path_audit_20260715.md`.

### 2026-07-15 STATIC: melee belongs at two native dispatcher callsites

The retained Player's queue owner is naturally scheduled: vtable
`0x142A6C2E8 +0x1E8` is
`PlayerMeleeController_DispatchQueuedButtonCommandsTick 0x141279DF0`, which reads
Player at owner `+0x108`, queue at `+0x150`, and calls
`DispatchPlayerMeleeButtonHoldReleaseAndGrappleReactionCommands 0x141272A50` once
per engine-clock stamp. Inside that dispatcher, the exact `melee-r1`
`PlayerInputCommandState_IsCommandActive 0x141E39D50` call is `0x141273AE2`; a
true result immediately builds the native payload and calls
`PushOrRotateMeleeCommandQueueEntry 0x141273FA0`.

The independent consumer side agrees: vtable `+0x220` is `0x14127A250`, which
hashes literal `melee-r1` and calls vtable `+0x1F8` (`0x141279E50`) to resolve the
command against the same queue and Player. The PC mouse branch is not suitable
for puppet injection because `Joypad_IsKeyboardMouseInputModeActive 0x14183E2D0`
gates it on `Joypad+0xBE1`, a field maintained by native input polling. The mouse
press call `0x141273D3B` remains useful only for capturing the local PC player's
original-true press.

Build `2026-07-15cq` therefore patches only `0x141273AE2` and `0x141273D3B` with
one nearby FF25 relay. It captures local mouse/R1 press into a 150 ms protocol
pulse and consumes one receiver-side atomic press only from retained slot 1's
`melee-r1` query. The rejected global PlayerInput detour, manual dispatcher,
direct queue push, and direct animation calls remain disabled. Release build
succeeds. Status: **STATIC / HYPOTHESIS ready for runtime**; full evidence,
competitors, and prediction are in
`reports/melee_native_callsite_relay_20260715.md`.

### 2026-07-15 STATIC: `g_spawn_captured` is a required remote-Player gate

The cp classification of spawn capture as production-unneeded diagnostics is
**REJECTED**. `spawn_capture_veh` is the sole writer of `g_spawn_captured` and
the descriptor/context consumed by `reissue_spawn_for_slot1`. The live-peer
auto-spawn condition at the Nadine update path explicitly requires that flag

is pending.

after restoring descriptor capture, with cq melee still parked. This rejects UDP,

and confirms the disabled spawn gate as the root cause. The enable flag was then

capture. Do not classify it as diagnostics again.

### 2026-07-15 STATIC: ADS body turn is `FgAnimData+0x1C0` world publication

The actual render boundary is now resolved. `FgDrawManager_PrepareInstanceForRendering
0x14181A9B0` has exact `fg-draw-mgr.cpp` source assertions, copies CPU skinning
matrices from `FgAnimData+0x230` to upload storage `+0x240`, and independently
calls `FgAnimData_GetRenderWorldMatrix 0x1403014F0`. The getter reads the 64-byte
world matrix at `FgAnimData+0x1C0` (optionally multiplied by `+0x2E0`).

`FgAnimData_PublishWorldTransform 0x1418C55D0` converts a 32-byte
translation+quaternion block, applies the FgAnimData scale, and publishes through
`FgAnimData_PublishWorldMatrix 0x1418C54D0`. The stock animation-manager phase
`0x40` callsite at `0x141A8FC00` proves ABI `rcx=FgAnimData`, `rdx=transform`,
`r8b=0`. This explains the prior runtime rejection: changing `Player+0x140` could
track peer yaw in memory while the visible model retained the previously published
FgAnimData matrix. Whole-body ADS yaw belongs at this publication boundary, not in
all 651 joint matrices. Full evidence and falsifiable prediction are in
`reports/player_aim_fganim_world_transform_20260715.md`.

**Build cz REJECTED:** it wrote peer yaw to block `+0x00`; the remote model then
disappeared immediately on ADS with every weapon. Exact assembly proves `+0x00`
is translation and `+0x10` is quaternion: `0x1418C55F8` passes `+0x10` into the
quaternion-to-matrix math while original `+0x00` supplies the translation row,
and the phase caller stores position/orientation to those same adjacent slots.
Build da preserves `+0x00` and replaces only quaternion `float[4..7]`.
